metadata.description: Use Toolaze free AI Clothes Changer online to change outfits from one photo. Upload a picture, describe clothes, preview virtual try-on ideas, and keep edits fully clothed.

hero.desc: Upload a person photo and choose a built-in clothing reference, or use Custom to upload your own clothing reference and add optional directions. Preview realistic AI outfit changes for business, formal, swimwear, creator, and product styling.

safetyNotice: This tool is for tasteful outfit edits and adult swimwear previews only. Use photos you own or have permission to edit, and avoid requests that remove clothing, sexualize a person, impersonate someone, or misuse branded uniforms and logos.

intro.title: What Is an AI Clothes Changer?

content.title: Preview outfit ideas without a reshoot
content.text: An AI clothes changer edits the visible clothing in a person photo while keeping the person, pose, lighting, and scene as stable as possible. Upload the person as image 1, then choose a built-in outfit or upload a clothing reference as image 2. Custom mode uses the same two-image workflow and lets you add precise directions for fabric, color, fit, coverage, or occasion.

content.title: Built for clothing references and custom prompts
content.text: Choose Women or Men for a fast start with a curated full-body clothing reference. Use Custom when you have your own clothing reference and want to add optional styling directions. Treat the output as a visual preview. Fine fabric labels, exact brand logos, hidden seams, and physically impossible layering can still need manual review.

howToUse.title: How to Change Clothes with AI

steps.title: Upload the person photo
steps.desc: Use image 1 for the person. Choose a clear full-body or half-body photo where the current outfit, arms, torso, and body outline are visible.

steps.title: Choose or upload a clothing reference
steps.desc: Choose a built-in outfit in Women or Men, or open Custom and upload your own clothing reference as image 2. In Custom, add optional directions when you need to clarify fabric, color, fit, coverage, or occasion.

steps.title: Generate and refine
steps.desc: Check whether the face, body proportions, hands, background, and clothing coverage stayed stable. If needed, add constraints such as preserve pose, keep face unchanged, match image 2 clothing, realistic fabric folds.

photoTips.title: Photo Tips for Better Outfit Changes
photoTips.subtitle: AI clothing edits work best when the reference image clearly shows the person and the garment area you want to replace.

items.title: Show the full outfit area
items.desc: Full-body or waist-up photos usually work better than tight face crops because the model can read sleeves, hem lines, hands, and body position.

items.title: Use simple poses first
items.desc: Straightforward standing or seated poses are easier than crossed arms, covered torsos, motion blur, mirrors, or heavy occlusion.

items.title: Keep identity constraints explicit
items.desc: Include preserve face, hair, skin tone, pose, body proportions, background, and lighting when you need a clean virtual try-on preview.

items.title: Avoid tiny text and exact logos
items.desc: Small brand marks, badges, labels, and embroidery may distort. Use fictional logos or plain garments unless you own and need the specific asset.

faq.q: Can I use Toolaze as a free AI clothes changer?
faq.a: Yes. Toolaze provides an online AI clothes changer workflow for quick outfit previews. Availability and generation limits may depend on the current Toolaze access policy shown in the product.

faq.q: Is this the same as virtual try-on?
faq.a: It is virtual try-on style image editing: upload a person photo and describe the clothes you want to preview. It is useful for visual ideas, but it should not replace real garment fitting, sizing, or final product photography.

faq.q: What kind of photo works best?
faq.a: Use a clear full-body or half-body photo with visible clothing, simple pose, good lighting, and minimal occlusion. Photos with crossed arms, cropped torsos, hidden hands, or heavy blur are harder to edit cleanly.

faq.q: Can I change only the shirt, dress, jacket, or pants?
faq.a: Yes. Say exactly which garment to replace and what must stay unchanged. For example: change only the jacket to a navy blazer, keep the shirt, face, hair, pose, and background unchanged.

faq.q: Can I use brand logos or uniforms?
faq.a: Use brand marks, uniforms, or protected designs only when you own the rights or have permission. For general previews, plain garments and fictional logos are safer and usually render more cleanly.

faq.q: Does the tool support clothing removal?
faq.a: No. Use the tool only for tasteful, fully clothed outfit edits. Do not use it to remove clothing, create sexualized images, impersonate someone, or edit a person without appropriate permission.
